options: By evening I’ll already have finished the report
In the evening I’ll be writing the report
I’ve probably already finished the report
items.explanation: -miş is the checkmark, ol-acağım is a moment in the future. By evening it’s all done.

options: At ten I’ll go to bed
At ten I’ll already be awake
items.explanation: -iyor is a process. At ten the sleep is already going on. “I’ll go to bed” would be uyuyacağım.
The light is off: that’s a clue. -mış olmalı is a conclusion: he must have left already.

options: Ali has to come at five
Ali will be coming at five
items.explanation: Without -mış ol- it’s an obligation. Gelmeli means “has to come.”
Look at the end: ol-acak is a future moment, ol-malı is a guess. Then the middle: -mış means already, -iyor means ongoing.

items.translation: By evening we’ll already have finished.
items.explanation: The -miş checkmark goes on the verb, the person -acağız goes on ol-. Akşama kadar bitirmiş olacağız.
Person goes on once, and only on ol-. The first part is just varmış.

items.translation: At eight the movie will already have started.
items.explanation: “Already” is -mış. The last vowel in başla is a, so -mış.

exercises.instruction: Samsun bus station board: pick the sign with the form
exercises.description: The board shows a situation and the start of a sentence. The learner picks one of three signs: -mış olacak, -iyor olacak or -mış olmalı. The board flips its letters and shows the full sentence. The logic is in index.html.

items.ru: By nine the bus will already have reached Samsun.
items.explanation: Done by then: varmış olacak.

items.ru: At ten I’ll be walking along the waterfront.
items.explanation: At ten the walk is going on: yürüyor olacağım.

items.ru: Ayşe isn’t answering. She’s probably fallen asleep.
items.explanation: There’s a clue, no witnesses: uyumuş olmalı.

items.ru: By lunch we’ll already have climbed Amisos Hill.
items.full: Öğlene kadar Amisos Tepesi'ne çıkmış olacağız.
items.explanation: By lunch we’re already at the top: çıkmış olacağız.

items.ru: Don’t call at three: I’ll be in a taxi to the airport.
items.full: Saat üçte taksiyle havalimanına gidiyor olacağım.
items.explanation: At three the ride is in progress: gidiyor olacağım.

items.ru: The display case is empty. Looks like the pide is gone.
items.explanation: An empty case is a clue. Conclusion: bitmiş olmalı.

exercises.instruction: Say it yourself: type the form

items.translation: This time tomorrow I’ll be sleeping.
items.explanation: Sleep in progress means -iyor: uyu + yor = uyuyor.

items.translation: By now he should already be home.
items.explanation: A guess about something done is -miş olmalı. gel has the vowel e, so -miş.

items.translation: By evening I’ll already have finished the report.
items.explanation: Future moment and “I” go on ol-: olacağım.

items.prompt: How do you say “This time tomorrow we’ll be waiting for you”?
options: Yarın bu saatte seni bekliyor olacağız.
Yarın bu saatte seni beklemiş olacağız.
items.explanation: The waiting is going on at that moment. A process: -iyor olacağız.

items.statement: “Ali gelmiş olmalı” means “Ali has to come.”
items.explanation: With -mış it’s a guess: Ali must have come already. “Has to come” is gelmeli.

items.text: Hazirana kadar bu kursu tamamla___ olacağız.
items.translation: By June we’ll already have finished this course.
items.explanation: Done by June means -mış. The last vowel is a, so -mış.

items.prompt: Which one is right for “we’ll already have arrived”?
items.explanation: Checkmark on the verb, tense and person on ol-: varmış olacağız.

items.prompt: The light is off, no shoes by the door. What do you say about your neighbor?
items.explanation: The clues say: already gone. The guess is çıkmış olmalı.
